items.prompt:
A class presentation calls for:
A) formal English
B) slang
C) silence

Talking casually with friends is:
A) informal speech
B) always formal
C) not allowed

Formal speech avoids:
A) slang
B) complete sentences
C) clear words

In a job interview, 'Yeah, I'm like super good at that stuff' should become:
A) 'Yes, I am very skilled in that area.'
B) 'Yeah, totally.'
C) 'For sure, dude.'
items.answer: A) 'Yes, I am very skilled in that area.'

solution.answer: A) 'Yes, I am very skilled in that area.'

items.prompt:
When is INFORMAL speech appropriate?
A) in casual settings like talking with friends
B) in a formal debate
C) in a job interview
items.answer: A) in casual settings like talking with friends

solution.answer: A) in casual settings like talking with friends

items.prompt:
Adapting your speech to context means:
A) matching your language to the audience and situation
B) always using slang
C) always speaking the same way
items.answer: A) matching your language to the audience and situation

steps: Fit the setting. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) matching your language to the audience and situation

items.prompt:
Which sentence is MOST appropriate for a formal speech to the school board?
A) 'Our proposal would improve safety for all students.'
B) 'This idea is gonna be awesome, trust me.'
C) 'Yeah so basically it's cool.'
items.answer: A) 'Our proposal would improve safety for all students.'

steps: Formal, complete, no slang. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) 'Our proposal would improve safety for all students.'

items.prompt:
Why is being able to switch between formal and informal English a valuable skill?
A) different contexts call for different registers, and using the right one is effective
B) formal is always better everywhere
C) informal is never useful
items.answer: A) different contexts call for different registers, and using the right one is effective

steps: Match register to context. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) different contexts call for different registers, and using the right one is effective
